points.description: Initialisation: the neurons/weights are arranged in the required topological lattice and the weights are set to random values (all different). Equivalent wording, e.g. 'set up the grid and initialise weights randomly', earns the mark.

Iterative learning loop, in the correct order: sample an input from the input space; find the winning neuron by similarity matching (closest weight vector); update the winner and its neighbours using the neighbourhood function; decay the learning rate and shrink the neighbourhood radius; repeat until ordering and convergence are reached, otherwise keep sampling. The mark requires the winner-finding and the neighbourhood weight update, plus the loop/stopping idea. Equivalent wording and alternative stopping criteria (e.g. a fixed number of epochs) earn the mark.
